literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, Xiao Dahuan
idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, and Xiao Dahuan

literal: Biographies 17
idiomatic: Biographies 17

literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, great-grandson Yi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, nephew Zan, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, Xiao Dahuan
idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, great-grandson Yi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu, Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, nephew Zan, Xiao Zhengbiao, Xiao Zhi, Xiao Tui, Xiao Tai, Xiao Hui, Xiao Yuansu, and Xiao Dahuan

literal: Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was a man of Wen in Henei, a descendant of Prince of Qiao Jin, youngest brother of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was from Wen in Henei, descended from Prince Jin of Qiao, youngest brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.

literal: After the Jin crossed the Yangzi, Jin's descendants inherited the fief of Prince of Qiao.
idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, the line of Prince Jin held the Qiao title in succession.

literal: By Xiuzhi's time his father Tian was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Yan Provinces.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi's father Tian was General Who Pacifies the North and dual Inspector of Qing and Yan.

literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Xiuzhi was Inspector of Jing Province; driven out by Huan Xuan, he fled to Murong De.
idiomatic: In Tianxing year 5 he governed Jing until Huan Xuan expelled him and he fled to Murong De.

literal: When Xuan was executed, he returned to Jiankang and again became Inspector of Jing.
idiomatic: After Xuan's death he returned to Jiankang and resumed the Jing inspectorship.

literal: Xiuzhi had won considerable favor among the people of the Jiang and Han region.
idiomatic: He had won deep goodwill along the Jiang and Han.

literal: His son Wensi succeeded his elder brother Shangzhi as Prince of Qiao and plotted against Liu Yu.
idiomatic: His son Wensi succeeded elder brother Shangzhi as Prince of Qiao and plotted against Liu Yu.

literal: Yu seized Xiuzhi and sent him forward, making him act at Yu's bidding.
idiomatic: Yu seized him and used him as his instrument.

literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to depose Wensi and also wrote Yu a letter of apology.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi petitioned to depose Wensi and wrote Yu apologizing.

literal: In the Shenrui era Yu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his nephew Wenzu and killed them, then marched against Xiuzhi.
idiomatic: In Shenrui, Yu killed Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and nephew Wenzu, then attacked Xiuzhi.

literal: Xiuzhi with Lu Zongzhi and Zongzhi's son Gui raised troops to attack Yu.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi joined Lu Zongzhi and Zongzhi's son Gui in arms against Yu.

literal: Defeated, he fled with his son Wensi and Zongzhi to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: Beaten, he fled with Wensi and Zongzhi to Yao Xing.

literal: When Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi with Wensi and several hundred men including Jin Prince of Hejian Zidaosi all brought wives and children and surrendered to Changsun Song.
idiomatic: When Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi, Wensi, Prince Zidaosi of Hejian, and hundreds more surrendered to Changsun Song with their families.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Grand General Who Conquers the West, Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, Duke of Shiping, posthumous name Sheng.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Grand General Who Conquers the West, Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, Duke of Shiping, posthumous name Sheng.

literal: Wensi was at odds with Duke of Huainan Guo Fan and Pool-Yang Zidaosi, yet feigned closeness with them.
idiomatic: Wensi disliked Duke Guo Fan of Huainan and Zidaosi of Chiyang but pretended friendship.

literal: Guo Fan was blunt by nature; drunk, he wished to defect outward.
idiomatic: Guo Fan was blunt; drunk once, he meant to flee.

literal: Wensi reported them; all were executed for the crime.
idiomatic: Wensi informed; all were put to death.

literal: Wensi was made Minister of Justice and enfeoffed Duke of Yulin.
idiomatic: Wensi became Minister of Justice and Duke of Yulin.

literal: Wensi was skilled in his office; in hearing cases the people could not hide their circumstances.
idiomatic: He excelled at his post; in court the people could not conceal the facts.

literal: Advanced to Prince of Qiao, he held the post of General Who Pacifies the Wilderness and died.
idiomatic: He rose to Prince of Qiao and General Who Pacifies the Wilderness, then died.

literal: Sima Chuzhi, styled Dexiu, was an eighth-generation descendant of Grand Commandant Kui, younger brother of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, styled Dexiu, was eight generations from Grand Commandant Kui, Jin Emperor Xuan's younger brother.

literal: His father Rongqi was Jin Inspector of Yi Province and was killed by his aide Yang Chengzu.
idiomatic: His father Rongqi, Jin's Yi Inspector, was killed by aide Yang Chengzu.

literal: Chuzhi was then seventeen; he escorted his father's coffin back to Danyang.
idiomatic: Chuzhi was seventeen and bore his father's coffin back to Danyang.

literal: When Liu Yu exterminated the Sima clan, his uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi were both killed.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu purged the Simas, uncle Xuanqi and brother Zhenzhi perished.

literal: Chuzhi fled and hid among monks, crossed the river to the Ru and Ying region.
idiomatic: He hid among monks, crossed the river, and reached the Ru–Ying country.

literal: Chuzhi from youth had heroic spirit and could humble himself to treat scholars.
idiomatic: From youth he had heroic bearing and knew how to win men by courtesy.

literal: When Song received the mandate, he planned revenge.
idiomatic: When the Song took the throne he plotted vengeance.

literal: He gathered followers and held Changshe; those who came to him often numbered more than ten thousand.
idiomatic: He held Changshe with more than ten thousand followers.

literal: Emperor Wu of Song feared him deeply and sent the assassin Mu Qian to plot his death.
idiomatic: Song's Emperor Wu sent the assassin Mu Qian against him.

literal: Chuzhi treated Qian with great kindness.
idiomatic: Chuzhi treated Qian with exceptional kindness.

literal: Qian feigned illness by night, knowing Chuzhi would surely come, intending to kill him when he did.
idiomatic: Qian feigned sickness at night, sure Chuzhi would visit and meaning to strike then.

literal: Hearing Qian was ill, Chuzhi indeed brought soup and medicine himself to visit him.
idiomatic: Hearing of the illness, Chuzhi came in person with soup and medicine.

literal: Qian was moved by his intent, produced a dagger from beneath the mat, told the whole plan, and thereupon devoted himself to serve him.
idiomatic: Moved, Qian drew the dagger from under the mat, confessed the plot, and served him thereafter.

literal: His pushing sincerity and trusting things—winning men's hearts—were all of this kind.
idiomatic: Winning hearts by sincerity was always his way.

literal: At the end of Mingyuan, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin overran Henan; Chuzhi sent envoys to surrender and was made Inspector of Jing.
idiomatic: Late in Mingyuan, Duke Xi Jin of Shanyang took Henan; Chuzhi surrendered and was made Jing Inspector.

literal: When Xi Jin had pacified Henan, Chuzhi's following in households was distributed into the four commanderies Runan, Ruyang, Nandun, and Xincai to enlarge Yu Province.
idiomatic: After Henan fell, his households were split among Runan, Ruyang, Nandun, and Xincai to swell Yu.

literal: At the beginning of Taiwu, Chuzhi sent wife and children to live within at Ye.
idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he sent family to live inside at Ye.

literal: Soon summoned to court, he was made Grand General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed Prince of Langye, to resist the Song army.
idiomatic: Soon at court he was Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Langye against Song.

literal: He was granted front and rear guard musicians.
idiomatic: He received front and rear guard musicians.

literal: He defeated a detached force of the Song general Dao Yanzhi at Changshe.
idiomatic: He routed Song general Dao Yanzhi's detached force at Changshe.

literal: Again with Champion An Qi he stormed and took Huatai, capturing Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo, with more than ten thousand prisoners.
idiomatic: With Champion An Qi he took Huatai, capturing Zhu Xiuzhi, Li Yuande, Dongjun's Shen Mo, and over ten thousand men.

literal: He memorialized asking to advance further in attack; Taiwu, because the army had long been weary, did not agree and recalled him as Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He asked to press the attack; Taiwu, the troops weary, refused and recalled him as Regular Attendant.

literal: Song generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi invaded Chouchi.
idiomatic: Song generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi attacked Chouchi.

literal: Chuzhi with Duke of Huainan Pi Baozi and others supervised the Guanzhong armies, routed Fangming, and captured Chongzhi.
idiomatic: Chuzhi with Duke Pi Baozi of Huainan commanded Guanzhong forces, routed Fangming, and took Chongzhi.

literal: Chouchi was pacified and he returned.
idiomatic: Chouchi pacified, he returned.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against the Rouran, Chuzhi with Duke of Jiyin Lu Zhongshan and others supervised transport to follow the great army.
idiomatic: On the Rouran campaign Chuzhi with Duke Lu Zhongshan of Jiyin directed supply trains for the main host.

literal: At the time General Who Pacifies the North Feng Dang had fled into the Rouran and urged them to strike Chuzhi to cut off grain transport.
idiomatic: General Feng Dang had fled to the Rouran and urged them to hit Chuzhi and sever supplies.

literal: The Rouran then sent scouts to Chuzhi's army, cut off donkeys' ears, and left.
idiomatic: The Rouran scouted his camp, clipped donkeys' ears, and withdrew.

literal: When someone reported the lost donkeys' ears, Chuzhi said: "Surely the scouts cut them as proof—the enemy is coming.
idiomatic: Told of the clipped ears, Chuzhi said, "Scouts took them as proof—the foe is near.

literal: " He then felled willows for a wall, poured water to freeze it; the wall stood and the enemy came but could not storm it and scattered.
idiomatic: He felled willows, flooded them to ice a wall; when the enemy came they could not breach it and broke away.

literal: Taiwu heard and praised him.
idiomatic: Taiwu heard and praised him.

literal: Soon he was given acting credentials, made Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand General of the Yunzhong Garrison, and Inspector of Shuo.
idiomatic: Soon acting credentials, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies, Yunzhong commander, and Shuo Inspector.

literal: At the beginning of Jinlong he married the daughter of Grand Commandant and Duke of Longxi Yuan He.
idiomatic: In Jinlong's opening he wed Grand Commandant Yuan He's daughter, Duchess of Longxi.

literal: He had sons Yanzong, next Zuan, next Yue.
idiomatic: Sons Yanzong, then Zuan, then Yue.

literal: Later he took a Juqu wife and had son Huiliang—that was the daughter of Hexi King Juqu Mujian, born of Taiwu's sister Princess Wuwei.
idiomatic: Later a Juqu wife bore Huiliang—daughter of King Juqu Mujian of Hexi, child of Taiwu's sister Princess Wuwei.

literal: Favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, Huiliang therefore inherited.
idiomatic: Favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, Huiliang inherited the house.

literal: By precedent he was reduced to duke; implicated in Mu Tai's crime he lost his title and died.
idiomatic: Reduced by precedent to duke, implicated in Mu Tai's affair he lost rank and died.

literal: Yue, styled Qingzong, rose to Inspector of Yu Province.
idiomatic: Yue, styled Qingzong, became Inspector of Yu.

literal: At the time there was one Dong Maonu of Shangcai in Runan, carrying five thousand cash.
idiomatic: In Runan's Shangcai a man named Dong Maonu carried five thousand cash.

literal: He died on the road.
idiomatic: He died on the road.

literal: The commandery and county people suspected Zhang Di of robbery; at Di's house they also found five thousand cash; Di, fearing torture, falsely confessed to murder.
idiomatic: Locals suspected Zhang Di; five thousand cash was found at his house; fearing torture he confessed murder.

literal: At the province Yue studied his expression and doubted it was true.
idiomatic: At the province Yue read his face and doubted the confession.

literal: He summoned Maonu's elder brother Lingzhi and said: "In killing for money one is flustered at the time and ought to leave something behind—what did you get?
idiomatic: He summoned brother Lingzhi: "A killer in haste leaves something—what was it?

literal: Lingzhi said: "Only a knife-handle plane.
idiomatic: Lingzhi said, "Only a knife-handle plane.

literal: " Yue took it to look and said: "This is not the work of a lane thug.
idiomatic: Yue inspected it: "No alley thug made this.

literal: He then summoned knife-makers within the province to show it.
idiomatic: He called the province's blade-makers.

literal: One before the Guo Gate said: "This plane was made by the gate artisan; last year it was sold to Guo townsman Dong Jizu.
idiomatic: One at the Guo Gate said a gate artisan made it and sold it last year to Dong Jizu.

literal: Yue seized Jizu and interrogated him; Jizu confessed in full.
idiomatic: Yue seized Jizu; he confessed everything.

literal: Lingzhi also found on Jizu's person the black jacket Maonu had worn; Jizu was executed by law.
idiomatic: On Jizu Lingzhi found Maonu's black jacket; Jizu was executed.

literal: Yue's scrutiny of prisons was often of this kind.
idiomatic: Yue's prison work was often thus.

literal: Soon with General Who Pacifies the South Yuan Ying he stormed Yiyang; an edict changed Liang's Si Province to Ying Province and made Yue its inspector.
idiomatic: Soon with Yuan Ying he took Yiyang; Liang's Si became Ying and Yue was made inspector.

literal: Changed to Inspector of Yu Province;
idiomatic: He was shifted to Inspector of Yu;

literal: for former merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yuyang.
idiomatic: for past merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yuyang.

literal: In the first year of Yongping, the city man Bai Zaosheng plotted rebellion and beheaded Yue's head to send to Liang.
idiomatic: Yongping year 1, Bai Zaosheng rebelled and sent Yue's head to Liang.

literal: An edict had Yang Province transfer a reward for Yue's head; he was posthumously made Inspector of Qing, posthumous name Zhuangzi.
idiomatic: Yang Province was ordered to ransom the head; posthumously Qing Inspector, posthumous name Zhuangzi.

literal: Son Fei inherited.
idiomatic: Son Fei inherited.

literal: Fei married Emperor Xuanwu's sister Princess Huayang, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards and Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Fei wed Princess Huayang, sister of Xuanwu, and became Commandant of Horse Guards and supernumerary attendant.

literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Cang.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Cang Inspector.

literal: Son Hong, styled Qingyun, was rough and martial by nature.
idiomatic: Son Hong, styled Qingyun, was rough and martial.

literal: He inherited the title, held the post of Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, and was sentenced to death for communicating with Western Wei.
idiomatic: He inherited, served as Commissioner of Waterways, and was executed for ties to Western Wei.

literal: Son Xiaozheng inherited.
idiomatic: Son Xiaozheng inherited.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent he was reduced in rank.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his rank was reduced by precedent.

literal: Fei's younger brother Yi.
idiomatic: Fei's younger brother Yi.

literal: Yi, styled Zunyin, was orphaned young and had resolve and conduct.
idiomatic: Yi, styled Zunyin, was orphaned young but steadfast.

literal: He began as staff officer in the Minister of State's office, later became Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He began in the Minister of State's office, later supernumerary attendant.

literal: In the third year of Datong, when the great army recovered Hongnong, he at Wencheng offered allegiance and returned to Western Wei.
idiomatic: Datong 3, when Hongnong was recovered, he submitted at Wencheng to Western Wei.

literal: In the sixth year he was made Inspector of Northern Xu Province.
idiomatic: Year 6 he became Northern Xu Inspector.

literal: In the eighth year he entered court.
idiomatic: Year 8 he came to court.

literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised him and especially rewarded and comforted him.
idiomatic: Zhou's Emperor Wen praised and specially rewarded him.

literal: Before long, more than four thousand households in Henei came over—all Yi's old neighbors—and he was ordered to lead as Administrator of Henei to settle the displaced.
idiomatic: Soon four thousand Henei households, his old neighbors, submitted; he was made Henei magistrate to settle refugees.

literal: In the fifteenth year Zhou Wen ordered that righteous leaders east of the mountains who could lead crowds through the Pass would all receive added rewards.
idiomatic: Year 15 Zhou Wen promised added reward to eastern leaders who could bring men through the Pass.

literal: Yi led a thousand households first to arrive; Zhou Wen wished to enfeoff Yi for it.
idiomatic: Yi brought a thousand households first; Wen meant to enfeoff him for it.

literal: Yi declined: "Men who rise in righteousness and return from afar to the imperial transformation all do so from sincere hearts within—how could Yi lead them?
idiomatic: Yi declined: "Righteous men who return from afar act from their own hearts—how could I lead them?

literal: To enfeoff Yi now would be to sell righteous men for glory.
idiomatic: Enfeoffing me now would be buying glory with righteous men.

literal: Zhou Wen approved and followed his wish.
idiomatic: Wen approved and let it pass.

literal: He was made Commander-in-Chief and his wife Yuan was made Princess of Xiangcheng Commandery.
idiomatic: He was made Commander-in-Chief; his wife Yuan became Princess of Xiangcheng.

literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was made Inspector of Ba Province, advanced to Commissioner with credentials, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, advanced to Baron of Langye.
idiomatic: At Xiaomin's accession he was Ba Inspector, then Commissioner, Agile Cavalry Grand General, Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies, Baron of Langye.
